tasks.short: Read the surgery notes, discuss the pet's post-operative status with the owner, explain home care and medication, prepare the discharge instructions, give them to the owner and note the talk in the record.

steps.what: Veterinary technician reads the record and surgery notes before talking to the owner
Veterinary technician discusses the medical health of the pet with the owner, such as post-operative status
Veterinary technician explains home care and medication at discharge
Veterinary technician writes the discharge instructions by hand
Veterinary technician checks the final instructions against the vet's orders and this pet: medicines, doses, times, wound care and the owner's e-mail address
Veterinary technician gives the owner the discharge instructions: a handwritten copy today, printed and e-mailed from the record after the change
Veterinary technician notes the conversation with the owner in the record

tasks.design: The practice system ({OTHER}) shows the surgery notes, medication and vet's orders on one screen. Discharge instructions come from a template per procedure filled with the pet's medication and dose from the vet's orders; the technician adds what is particular to this pet, checks the final text and the owner's address, and then prints and e-mails it once from the record. Contact notes are written as today. Talking with the owner and explaining home care stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Discharge instructions were handwritten for every pet and notes typed in free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice systems fill discharge templates from the vet's orders and e-mail them to owners.
tasks.still_hard: Worried owners need time, not paper.
tasks.human_edge: Showing an anxious owner how to give a tablet to a cat.

reach.learn: Whether owners call back less with questions.

evidence.claim: Practice management systems can fill discharge templates from treatment records and e-mail them to owners.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient record to the contact note; the follow-up visit is outside.
Input contract: surgery notes and orders by the vet; templates kept by the practice; fallback is handwriting.
Owners read printed or e-mailed instructions as they read handwritten ones; no added owner time.

Talking with owners, the final check and the contact note keep their full time. s1 keeps 70 because notes and orders sit on one screen and reading stays; s4 keeps 60 because the template gives the standard home care text and medicines from the orders, and the technician still writes what is particular; s5 keeps 50 because printing replaces copying by hand and handing over stays.
research_questions: Do owner calls after discharge fall?

incremental.description: Veterinary technician updates discharge templates with the vets.

approvals.approved_version: The discharge instructions with medicines, doses, times and home care exactly as checked by the technician in s4b against the vet's orders, printed for the owner and e-mailed once to the owner's address in the record; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: templates fit few procedures, so most instructions are still written and s4 keeps 85 (7.8); high: a template for each common procedure (10.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Copy lab results into records, record treatments and medicines given, count pharmaceuticals and supplies, and log equipment checks.

steps.what: Veterinary technician copies laboratory results from analyser printouts into the patient record; after the change checks that each in-house result landed in the right record and copies results from outside labs
Veterinary technician records treatments and medicines given in the treatment records
Veterinary technician counts pharmaceuticals and supplies on the shelves
Veterinary technician logs equipment checks and calibrations in a paper logbook

tasks.design: In-house analysers send results straight into the patient record in the practice system ({OTHER}). Medicines given are picked from the stock list on the treatment sheet, which takes the same time as writing them and books them off stock, so shelf counts become spot checks. Equipment checks are logged on a recurring task list that shows which are due.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were copied from printouts and stock counted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Veterinary analysers link to practice systems.
tasks.still_hard: Medicines used without booking make stock levels drift.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing a vaccine runs short before the spring rush.
tasks.altitude: The technician checks proposals and exceptions instead of copying and counting.

evidence.claim: Veterinary analysers can send results into practice management systems.
In three labs, middleware rules lifted autoverification of results from 40-60% to over 90%.
Veterinary practices must keep records of veterinary medicines administered and dispensed.

assumptions: Boundary: from analyser printouts and treatments to the equipment log; ordering is outside.
Input contract: results from in-house analysers; stock list from the wholesaler; fallback is printouts.

Shelf counts become spot checks, so s3 keeps 60 because supplies not booked from the treatment sheet are still counted. Recording treatments keeps its full time; s1 keeps 20 for checking in-house results and copying outside lab results; s6 keeps 90 because only finding which checks are due goes, and writing each result stays.
Results from outside labs still arrive by e-mail.
unknowns: Analysers linked to the practice system.

incremental.description: Veterinary technician books off medicines used without the treatment sheet.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older analysers have no link, so half of results are still copied and s1 keeps 60 (21.5); high: in-house analysers are linked as designed (33.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take booking calls, find slots, plan surgery and procedure days with the vet, enter bookings, confirm the next day's list, and remind owners with fasting instructions.

steps.what: Owner books an appointment: by phone today, online for routine visits after the change
Veterinary technician takes booking calls and finds a slot in the agenda
Veterinary technician schedules procedures for animals with the vet: theatre time, fasting and equipment
Veterinary technician enters the appointments in the practice agenda
Veterinary technician confirms the next day's appointment and procedure list
Veterinary technician checks each reminder: pet, time, the fasting instructions for the procedure and the owner's number and address
Veterinary technician sends owners reminders with fasting instructions: by phone today, by releasing the checked texts and e-mails after the change

tasks.design: Owners book routine appointments such as vaccinations and check-ups online in slots the practice opens in the agenda ({OTHER}); bookings land in the agenda without retyping. Surgery and procedure days are still planned by the technician with the vet. Once the technician has confirmed the next day's list, they check each reminder with the fasting instructions for its procedure and release them once to owners by text message and e-mail.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every booking came by phone and every reminder was a call.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice systems offer online booking and automatic reminders.
tasks.still_hard: Sick animals need triage by phone, not an online slot.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing on the phone that a booking is really an emergency.

reach.learn: Whether owners prefer online booking for routine visits.

evidence.claim: Veterinary practice systems offer online booking in open slots and automatic text and e-mail reminders.
Owner phone numbers and e-mail addresses used for reminders are personal data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the owner's request to the reminder sent; the visit itself is outside.
Input contract: open slots set by the practice; fasting texts per procedure from the vets; fallback is phone booking and calls.
Owners booking online spend about the same time as on the phone; this is priced in s1, which keeps its full time.
Planning procedure days, confirming the list and checking reminders keep their full time. Online booking covers about half of bookings, so s2 and s4 keep 50; s6 keeps 10 for the release.
research_questions: Do no-shows fall with automatic reminders?

incremental.description: Veterinary technician moves online bookings that need a longer slot.

approvals.approved_version: The next day's reminders per owner with pet, time and fasting instructions exactly as checked by the technician in s5b, sent once by text message and e-mail to the owner's number and address in the agenda; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most owners keep phoning, so s2 and s4 keep 80 (18.1); high: half of bookings move online (34.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Counsel owners on health care, behaviour and nutrition in consultations, answer phone and e-mail questions, calculate feeding amounts, write an advice summary and send it to the owner.

steps.what: Veterinary technician provides counseling on animal health care, behavior problems or nutrition in consultations
Owner phones or e-mails with a care or feeding question
Veterinary technician answers phone and e-mail questions on care and feeding
Veterinary technician calculates daily feeding amounts for a diet
Veterinary technician writes an advice summary for the owner

loop.input: The technician's dictated key points, the feeding amounts from the calculator and the practice's vetted care texts.
loop.output: A plain-language advice summary for the owner.
loop.check: Code checks every amount and dose against the calculator and the vet's orders and lists any advice sentence not found in the technician's key points; the technician reads the whole text against the consultation, resolves each listed sentence and writes unclear parts by hand.
loop.stop: Approved by the technician, or after two redrafts the technician writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each owner's advice combines several points; a fixed template reads as a form letter and leaves the joining to the technician.

steps.what: Veterinary technician checks the final summary: the advice matches the consultation, the amounts, and the owner's e-mail address
Veterinary technician e-mails the checked advice summary to the owner: by writing an e-mail today, by one release from the record after the change

tasks.design: The practice website ({CMS}) carries vetted care pages on vaccination, worming, diet and behaviour, which the technician links in replies and owners can read first. Feeding amounts come from a calculator using the pet's weight, life stage and the food's energy content. A bounded step drafts the advice summary from the technician's key points; code checks every amount and lists sentences not found in the key points. The technician reads the draft against the consultation, checks the final text and address, and releases it once by e-mail. Counselling in consultations stays with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every question was answered from scratch and advice summaries written by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice websites hold care pages; language models draft summaries from key points.
tasks.still_hard: Behaviour problems depend on the household, which a page cannot see.
tasks.human_edge: Helping an owner see that a dog's growling is fear, not anger.
tasks.altitude: The technician checks drafted summaries instead of writing each from scratch.

reach.task: Care for a pet at home
reach.learn: Whether owners follow written advice better.

evidence.claim: With an ambient scribe, Dutch GPs spent 42.7 seconds less on documentation per consultation; consultation length did not change.
Language models can draft a plain-language summary from key points.

assumptions: Boundary: from the owner's concern to the summary sent; treatment decisions are outside.
Input contract: care pages vetted by the vets; food energy content from the label or supplier; fallback is answering from scratch.
Owners read care pages instead of phoning for some questions; about the same time, priced as customer time.

Counselling in consultations and the final check keep their full time. s3 keeps 60 because owners read care pages first and replies link them; s4 keeps 30 for entering weight and food; s5 keeps 70 because the technician still writes the key points and reads the whole draft; s6 keeps 20 for the release.
research_questions: How much of a drafted summary does the technician change?

already_counted.description: Veterinary technician reads and approves each drafted summary.

incremental.description: Veterinary technician keeps care pages current with the vets.
Owners read the practice's care pages.

approvals.approved_version: The advice summary text with feeding amounts exactly as checked by the technician in s5b, e-mailed once to the owner's address in the practice system; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few owners read the care pages and drafts need much rewriting, so s3 keeps 80 and s5 keeps 85 (16.3); high: as designed (22.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The veterinary technician keeps talking with owners, planning procedures and counselling; copying results, counting stock, booking calls and handwritten instructions shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A technician with more time for animals and their owners.
